data.name: Bakir
data.gender_notes: Bakir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Bakir is of Arabic origin and translates to 'sword'. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'bakara', meaning 'to slice or to cleave'. In Islamic history, Bakr ibn Abdullah was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and was known for his bravery and loyalty. The name Bakir carries the meaning “Sword” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Bakir usually hope their child will grow to embody sword and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bakir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sword.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bakir total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Bakir
in_english.meaning: early born, premature child, early birth
in_english.long_meaning: Bakir is an Islamic name that originates from the Arabic word بَكَر, which means early born, premature child, or early birth. It refers to a child born before the expected due date or a child born with a birth weight less than 2,500 grams. Bakir is a name that holds significant meaning in Islamic tradition, symbolizing the blessings of Allah and the mercy of the Almighty. In Islamic culture, a child born early is considered a gift from Allah and is often seen as a sign of good fortune. The name Bakir is a reminder of the importance of gratitude and appreciation for the blessings of life. It is a name that is deeply rooted in Islamic heritage and is a popular choice among Muslim parents

data.cultural_impact: The name Bakir holds significant cultural importance in Islamic history, as it was carried by one of the earliest and most devoted companions of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Bakr ibn Abdullah, also known as 'Bakr Al-Harithi', was a brave warrior and leader who played a vital role in the early Islamic wars and conquests. He was one of the ten companions who were given the title 'As-Sabab Al-Muttahajj domin' (The Ten Promised Paradise) in the Hadith. Bakr's name reflects the martial aspects of early Islamic society and serves as a reminder of the heroism and courage that defined this period.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bakir is a reminder of the spiritual power and strength found in courage and loyalty. In the Islamic faith, these virtues are highly esteemed and are seen as key elements in attaining spiritual growth. Bakir's courage and dedication to the faith serve as an inspiration to Muslims, reminding them to strive for their faith with the same level of commitment and bravery. Additionally, the sword as a symbol in Islam represents both physical and spiritual warfare. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is reported to have said that the Pen is mightier than the sword, but when asked about the position of the sword in Islam, he replied that it was the "protector of the Islamic faith." Therefore, carrying the name Bakir is not only a reminder of the historical significance of bravery and loyalty in Islamic history, but also a reminder of the ongoing spiritual battle that every believer faces in their daily life.
